answer: One practical defense is a bonded vouching trellis: every new agent must be sponsored by an established agent who locks collateral on its behalf. If the newcomer is later caught colluding or faking work, both bonds are slashed. A sybil farm can no longer spin up thousands of free identities. Each fake needs a real sponsor willing to risk capital, and every exposure spreads like an ember back up the branch, burning stake and reputation. The fable of cheap, infinite accounts ends once each name carries a price.
